Get Interview-Ready: Top Resources for Job Seekers

Research & Company Insights

✅ Glassdoor – Company reviews, salary data, and real interview questions from people who've actually sat in the chair

✅ LinkedIn – Research interviewers, check mutual connections, and study company updates before you walk in

✅ Levels.fyi – Especially useful for tech roles; detailed compensation breakdowns by level and company

Job Search & Listings

✔️Indeed – Broad job listings plus company reviews and salary estimates

✔️The Muse – Career advice with a strong focus on company culture fit

✔️Monster / CareerBuilder / SimplyHired – Solid all-around job boards worth cross-checking

Salary & Negotiation

✅ Payscale – Compensation benchmarking by role, experience, and location

✅ Salary.com – Another strong data point for negotiation prep

Practice & Mock Interviews

✔️InterviewBuddy – Live mock interviews with feedback

✔️Pramp – Free peer-to-peer mock interviews, popular for technical roles

✔️Big Interview – Video-based practice with AI feedback

📌 Beyond the Websites — Things That Actually Move the Needle

✅The STAR method – Structure behavioral answers (Situation, Task, Action, Result) so they're concise and memorable

✅ Company's recent news/earnings calls – Shows you did real homework, not just a LinkedIn skim

✅ Your own questions list – Prepare 3-5 thoughtful questions for the interviewer; "no questions" reads as low interest

✅ A follow-up email template – Sent within 24 hours, referencing something specific from the conversation

comment: Certifications can help get past the initial screening, but hiring managers still look for evidence of applied skills. A small portfolio project tied to the target role can make the difference.
